plan.title: Author the gate plan

Write it to .agent-work/issue-467-trip-semantics/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope (attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'); surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. why_trail.why: Framed the ask against doctrine before touching source: the governor's Trip is a two-band CLI-boundary policy (SOFT advisory suffix on current, HARD pre-advance refusal) that is fail-safe on a missing reading, and the refresh-request/DIGEST reach-up flow it gates is the same primitive at every tier. #467 converts the HARD band from a refusal into a changed instruction; the schema doc says HARD refuses advance until a refresh-request keyed to the current why_ref exists, which is exactly the deadlock #431 reports since advance is what appends the why-record. No packet map exists, so my mission frame is sourced from schema/hook docs and will be verified against scripts/checklist_engine.py and scripts/gauge_reader.py at understand.

The trip's defect is a CHANNEL defect, not a permission defect. advance is the sole writer of why_trail (_append_why at checklist_engine.py:1899-1903), the latest live why-record IS the DIGEST (_digest:1139), and the DIGEST plus the ACTIVE line is the entire cold-start surface. HARD (_trip_hard_gate:1439) refuses that verb and the reach-up doctrine tells the tripped agent to file a refresh-request and go idle, so the understanding earned inside the tripping gate is never recorded anywhere. Fix direction: keep the band, move what it refuses -- permit the handoff-carrying advance so the why-record lands, and refuse the START of new work instead. DC6 is the bill: with no refusal there is no self-recording, so the engine must itself record whether a handoff artifact appeared before the next advance at an over-threshold gate.

PLAN IS FROZEN. Do not re-plan; execute it. Read in this order: .agent-work/issue-467-trip-semantics/execute.json (16 tasks, 5 gates -- drive it with the engine), CRITIC_TRIAGE.md (why the plan is shaped as it is), DIT_CONVERGENCE.md, MISSION_FRAME.md, PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md. THE DESIGN: HARD stops refusing 'advance' and refuses the verbs that BEGIN work (start, reopen -- NOT resume, which returns you to a gate you are already mid-way through). 'advance --why' already fails closed on silence and that --why already IS the DIGEST, so the governor was refusing the one verb that writes the handoff. That is #431, and fixing it costs zero new CLI surface, which is the best answer for #424 (blocked on this shape).
